concepts.title: Rise of the Gupta Empire and its Major Rulers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rise of the Gupta Empire and its Major Rulers' refers to.
questions.a: The Gupta dynasty founded around the 4th century CE in Magadha, whose major rulers Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Chandragupta II expanded territory and established a stable, prosperous empire often called a Golden Age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rise of the Gupta Empire and its Major Rulers'.
questions.a: The Guptas consolidated northern India through conquest, marriage alliances and efficient administration, beginning an era of cultural brilliance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rise of the Gupta Empire and its Major Rulers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Gupta Empire and its Rulers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gupta Administration and Governance' refers to.
questions.a: The Gupta system of government in which the king was the supreme authority, assisted by ministers, provincial governors and village councils, collecting land revenue and maintaining law and order.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gupta Administration and Governance'.
questions.a: A decentralised but effective administrative structure allowed local bodies to function while the emperor retained central control.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gupta Administration and Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Gupta Administration

concepts.title: The Golden Age of Art and Literature

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Golden Age of Art and Literature' refers to.
questions.a: The period of Gupta rule marked by outstanding achievements in Sanskrit literature, poetry, drama, sculpture, painting and architecture, earning the title Golden Age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Golden Age of Art and Literature'.
questions.a: Royal patronage and a stable, prosperous economy created conditions for a remarkable flowering of creative arts and letters.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Golden Age of Art and Literature' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Golden Age of Art and Literature

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature' refers to.
questions.a: Kalidasa, the foremost Sanskrit poet and dramatist of the Gupta court, whose works such as Shakuntalam, Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha represent the peak of classical Sanskrit literature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature'.
questions.a: Kalidasa's mastery of language, imagery and emotion made Sanskrit literature reach its classical high point under Gupta patronage.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Scientific Developments: Aryabhata and Varahamihira' refers to.
questions.a: Advances in mathematics and astronomy during the Gupta age led by scholars such as Aryabhata, who stated that the earth rotates and calculated pi, and Varahamihira, who wrote on astronomy and weather science.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Scientific Developments: Aryabhata and Varahamihira'.
questions.a: Gupta-era scholars made pioneering contributions to mathematics and astronomy that influenced later Indian and world science.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Scientific Developments: Aryabhata and Varahamihira' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Scientific Developments

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nalanda University' refers to.
questions.a: Nalanda, a great residential Buddhist monastery and centre of learning established near Rajgir in Bihar during the Gupta period, attracting scholars from many countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nalanda University'.
questions.a: Nalanda became a renowned international university offering instruction in religion, philosophy, logic and sciences, reflecting Gupta educational excellence.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nalanda University' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Nalanda University

concepts.title: Gupta Art and Architecture: The Ajanta Caves

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gupta Art and Architecture: The Ajanta Caves' refers to.
questions.a: The Gupta period produced remarkable art and architecture including temples with shikharas and the Ajanta caves, whose murals and sculptures are masterpieces of ancient Indian painting.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gupta Art and Architecture: The Ajanta Caves'.
questions.a: Gupta art combined religious themes with refined technique, producing enduring monuments such as the Ajanta cave paintings and early temples.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gupta Art and Architecture: The Ajanta Caves' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Gupta Art and Architecture

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Decline of the Gupta Empire' refers to.
questions.a: The gradual weakening and eventual collapse of Gupta power after the 6th century CE due to weak successors, invasions by the Hunas, administrative decentralisation and economic strain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Decline of the Gupta Empire'.
questions.a: A combination of external invasions and internal weaknesses ended the Gupta empire, even though its cultural legacy endured.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Decline of the Gupta Empire' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Decline of the Guptas
